sources.title: obra/superpowers
sources.quote: An agentic skills framework & software development methodology that works.
sources.claim: Biggest skills framework for developers: 293.6k stars, 26.3k forks on 2026-10-01. Stages: brainstorming, worktrees, plans, subagent-driven development, TDD, code review, finishing a branch.

sources.title: github/spec-kit
sources.quote: Toolkit to help you get started with SDD or any other process!
sources.claim: Spec-driven development toolkit: 139.7k stars, 12.5k forks on 2026-10-01. Commands constitution, specify, plan, tasks, implement. Aimed at developers.

sources.title: garrytan/gstack
sources.quote: Use Garry Tan's exact Claude Code setup
sources.claim: 134.6k stars, 20.1k forks on 2026-10-01. Roles: CEO, designer, eng manager, release manager, QA, security. Has review receipts and an evidence ledger. Aimed at developers who ship.

sources.title: bmad-code-org/BMAD-METHOD
sources.quote: turn an idea or change request into working software without giving up the thinking
sources.claim: 53.7k stars, 6.1k forks on 2026-10-01. Agile persona agents (product, architecture, UX, dev, testing). Requires Node.js, npm, git setup: aimed at developers.

sources.title: competitive-agents (Claude Code plugin by JayKim88)
sources.quote: Dual-agent competitive generation with cross-review, improvement rounds, and judge evaluation for plugin creation
sources.claim: Closest competitor to the arena idea: two agents, cross-review, a judge, the user picks. Limited to generating Claude Code plugins. No mechanical verification of claims, no penalty for lying.

sources.title: Lovable: $500M ARR, 146 staff, 80% non-technical builders
sources.quote: 80% of Lovable’s builders self-identify as non-technical.
sources.claim: Audience exists and pays: Lovable reports $500M ARR (self-reported) and 80% non-technical builders.

sources.title: The 70% problem: Hard truths about AI-assisted coding
sources.quote: They can get 70% of the way there surprisingly quickly, but that final 30% becomes an exercise in diminishing returns.
sources.claim: Named pain of non-engineers: the last 30%.

sources.title: Recent Frontier Models Are Reward Hacking
sources.quote: Instructing the model to solve the task the intended way, to not cheat, or to not reward hack had a nearly negligible effect on reward hacking
sources.claim: o3 reward-hacked in 39 of 128 RE-Bench runs (30.4%). Adding 'Please do not cheat.' left the rate at 80% (same as the original prompt) on one task. Prompts do not make agents honest; checks do.

sources.title: Building to the Test: Coding Agents Deliver What You Check, Not What You Requested
sources.quote: The agent does not, on its own, validate what it ships as a user would.
sources.claim: With a test oracle in the loop, agents hit near-perfect scores while the requested library was left dead or absent. Automated checks are necessary but not enough: someone must use the product like a user.

sources.title: AI Coding Agents Game Graders, Not Users
sources.quote: over 80% of rollouts from almost every frontier model contained reasoning about an imagined grader, and in 10-25% of cases, such reasoning pulled the agent's work away from the user's original specification
sources.claim: Agents optimise for an imagined grader. A rival who actively hunts for defects is a better reviewer than a friendly one.

sources.title: Claude 3.7 Sonnet and Claude Code
sources.quote: We discard patches that break the visible regression tests in the repository
sources.claim: Several parallel attempts, discard the ones that fail checks, rank the rest: 70.3% vs 63.7% on the same SWE-bench Verified subset. Scientific basis for the three-team arena.

sources.title: CVE-2025-48757
sources.quote: An insufficient database Row-Level Security policy in Lovable through 2025-04-15 allows remote unauthenticated attackers to read or write to arbitrary database tables of generated sites.
sources.claim: Vibe-coded apps leak data when nobody checks security. CVSS 9.3 critical. The developer agent needs a security checklist.

sources.title: Delving into LLM-assisted writing in biomedical publications through excess vocabulary
sources.quote: This excess word analysis suggests that at least 13.5% of 2024 abstracts were processed with LLMs.
sources.claim: AI writing has measurable fingerprint words ('delves' and others). Readers learn to spot them. Basis for the slop detector.

sources.title: Agent Skills overview
sources.publisher: Agent Skills (open standard, originally by Anthropic)
sources.quote: The Agent Skills format was originally developed by Anthropic, released as an open standard, and has been adopted by a growing number of agent products.
sources.claim: SKILL.md is portable: listed clients include Claude Code, Claude, Cursor, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot, VS Code, ChatGPT & Codex, Kiro, OpenCode, Goose and others.

sources.title: Claude Code docs: Subagents
sources.quote: By default, a subagent can spawn subagents of its own, up to three layers below the main conversation.
sources.claim: A manager subagent can launch its own developer and designer subagents (depth 2 of 3).

sources.title: Claude Code docs: Add components to a plugin
sources.quote: claude.ai and Cowork don't install a plugin that has a top-level bin/ directory
sources.claim: To stay installable in Cowork (the non-developer app), the plugin must not ship a top-level bin/ directory. Scripts go in scripts/ and are called via ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}.

sources.title: anthropics/skills: frontend-design SKILL.md
sources.quote: Spend your boldness in one place.
sources.claim: Names the five clusters of generic AI design (cream+serif+terracotta, dark+acid accent, broadsheet, SaaS card kit, template chrome). Basis for the designer's anti-template rules.

sources.title: Tall updates coming to Shorts
sources.quote: Starting on October 15, you can upload Shorts up to 3 minutes long.
sources.claim: Vertical videos can run up to 3 minutes on Shorts; our vertical cut stays under 60 s to also fit every other short-video feed.

sources.title: The 2026 AI Index Report
sources.quote: On a key coding benchmark—SWE-bench Verified—performance rose from 60% to near 100% in a single year.
sources.claim: Public coding benchmarks are saturated, so a founder needs per-project checks, not leaderboard scores.

sources.title: 2026 GenAI Code Security Report: AI Is Writing More of Your Code but Security Hasn't Caught Up
sources.quote: roughly 44% of AI code generation tasks introduced a risky security vulnerability in tests
sources.claim: Security did not improve with model capability, so the engine scans every verified commit and the developer works from a checklist.

sources.title: We Have a Package for You! A Comprehensive Analysis of Package Hallucinations by Code Generating LLMs
sources.quote: the average percentage of hallucinated packages is at least 5.2% for commercial models and 21.7% for open-source models
sources.claim: Models invent package names; the engine checks every dependency against its registry.

sources.title: AI | 2025 Stack Overflow Developer Survey
sources.quote: More developers actively distrust the accuracy of AI tools (46%) than trust it (33%)
sources.claim: Trust lags use; a product that replaces 'trust me' with a verdict on a commit meets the real gap.

sources.title: Time Horizon 1.1
sources.quote: We also report below the doubling time since 2024: this was at 109 days under TH1, and falls to 89 days under TH1.1.
sources.claim: Agents take on longer tasks every few months, so unattended runs need mechanical verification.

sources.title: Linux Foundation Announces the Formation of the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF)
sources.quote: founding contributions of leading technical projects including Anthropic’s Model Context Protocol (MCP), Block’s goose, and OpenAI’s AGENTS.md
sources.claim: Open agent standards consolidated; the repository ships AGENTS.md so any agent can follow its rules.

sources.title: Yes, August 2 Still Matters: The EU Approved a High-Risk AI Delay, but Most Transparency Obligations Remain
sources.quote: most relevant Article 50 deadlines remain August 2
sources.claim: Products that talk to people through AI must disclose it in the EU; the security checklist covers it.
